q: I want to create a contractor in SailPoint NERM via API. Which URL do I call and what does the body look like?
must: POST https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/profile (one) or /api/profiles (many) — NERM host, not api.identitynow.com
body is wrapped: {"profile": {...}} (or {"profiles": [...]})
profile_type_id and status are required; attributes is an object keyed by attribute uid
A: Call POST https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/profile (singular = one profile; POST /api/profiles takes {"profiles": [...]} for many). Not api.identitynow.com and not /non-employee-records (that is ISC NELM). Header Authorization: Bearer <ISC JWT> with scope nerm:api:profile-manager, nerm:api:integration-partner (create only) or nerm:general:manage. The body must be wrapped: {"profile": {"name": "Jane Doe", "profile_type_id": "<uuid of the Non-Employees profile type from GET /api/profile_types>", "status": "Active", "attributes": {"personal_first_name": "Jane", "personal_last_name": "Doe", "start_date": "01/15/2026", "organization": "<org profile id>"}}}. profile_type_id (an id, not a name) and status (Active, Inactive, On Leave, Terminated) are required. attributes are keyed by attribute uid (not label); text = string, profile/user select = target id (array if multi), dates in the attribute's date_format. Response: {"profile": {...}} with the new id. Sending the bare object is the classic 400; validation errors come as {"error":..., "errors": {"attr": "can't be blank"}}. Validate the body offline with scripts/check_nerm.py body.json.
B: Don't create the contractor by posting a bare record if you want NERM's normal processing (approvals, risk, notifications); the supported way is to start a Create workflow. For a direct insert, call POST https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/profiles with header Authorization: Bearer <NERM API token> and Content-Type: application/json. Body: {"profiles":[{"profile_type_id":"<uuid of the Contractor profile type>","status":"Active","attributes":{"personal_first_name":"Ada","personal_last_name":"Lovelace","email":"ada@vendor.com","start_date":"2026-12-01","end_date":"2027-06-30","organization":"<uuid of the Vendor profile>"}}]}. The attribute keys must be the attribute uids defined in Admin > Attributes. Reference attributes (vendor/organization, manager) take the UUID of the target profile or user. Get profile_type_id from GET /api/profile_types. To create through a workflow, use POST /api/workflow_sessions with workflow_id, requester_id and requester_type, plus the attributes.

q: How do I authenticate to the NERM API today? Can I use my ISC personal access token?
must: yes: exchange the ISC PAT (client credentials) at https://{isc-tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token and send the JWT as Bearer to NERM
legacy NERM API keys (Admin > System > Api) are deprecated and do not support scopes
tenants created after June 2025 must use ISC credentials (legacy keys not available); access follows the PAT owner's access/scopes
must_not: says the PAT client secret itself is sent as the bearer token
says only NERM API keys work
A: Yes, and that is now the recommended way. Create a personal access token (client id + secret) in ISC, exchange it with POST https://{isc-tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token using grant_type=client_credentials, client_id, client_secret, then send the returned access_token (a JWT) to NERM as Authorization: Bearer <JWT> on https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/.... The token carries the access of the ISC user who made the PAT and needs at least one nerm: scope (nerm:general:manage, nerm:api:read-only, nerm:api:profile-manager, etc.); it expires (expires_in, about 12.5 minutes in the guide's example), so refresh it. The PAT itself is not sent to NERM, only the JWT. Legacy NERM API keys (NERM Admin > System > Api) still exist but are deprecated, have no scopes, cannot be used by tenants created after June 2025 or by FedRAMP customers, and are not described in the OpenAPI security scheme.
B: NERM is a separate SaaS that lives at https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com, and its API has its own authentication. An ISC personal access token, or an ISC OAuth client_credentials token, will not work against /api. In NERM, create an API user/token: Admin > Settings (Advanced) > API Users / API Tokens. Pick the scopes, then copy the token, which is shown only once. Send it on every call as Authorization: Bearer <token>, with Accept: application/json and Content-Type: application/json. Tokens are long-lived bearer secrets, so store them in a vault and rotate them. Use one token per integration with least-privilege scopes. Calls without a valid token return 401, and calls with insufficient scope return 403. ISC credentials only come into play the other way round, in the ISC NERM source/connector configuration, where ISC calls NERM with the NERM token.

q: Which NERM API scope should I give an integration that only needs to start workflow sessions and read profiles, and what happens if a scope is missing?
must: nerm:api:workflow-operator (read profiles, profile types, workflows, advanced search; read and execute workflow sessions)
missing scope returns 403 with a generic error that does not name the scope
nerm:general:manage would work but grants full admin; scopes only exist on ISC tokens, not legacy keys
must_not: invents scopes like nerm:profiles:read or sp:scopes:all for this
A: Give the token only the scopes it needs. That means profile read (profiles:read, or 'Read' on Profiles) and workflow-session create (workflow_sessions:create, or 'Create' on Workflow Sessions). Do not grant write/update/delete on profiles, users, or admin objects. If the workflow reads profile types or workflows to resolve ids, add read on profile_types and workflows too. Scopes are fixed when the API token is created in NERM Admin > API. You usually cannot edit them in place, so you create a new token and revoke the old one. If a scope is missing, NERM rejects the call with HTTP 403 Forbidden (or 401 with an 'unauthorized/insufficient scope' message). Nothing is partially executed. Your integration should log the 403 and treat it as a configuration error, not something to retry.
B: Use nerm:api:workflow-operator. It gives read on profiles, profile types, workflows and advanced search, plus read and execute of workflow sessions, which is exactly 'start sessions and read profiles'. It is the only scope besides nerm:general:manage that can execute workflow sessions; nerm:api:profile-reader or nerm:api:read-only can read profiles but cannot run POST /workflow_sessions?run=true, and nerm:general:manage gives everything including system configuration (too much). Scopes only exist on ISC tokens (PAT exchanged at /oauth/token); legacy NERM API keys have no scopes. If a scope is missing, NERM returns 403 with a generic body {"error": "You do not have the permission to access this resource."} that never names the missing scope, so check the token's scopes first (scripts/check_nerm.py --scopes nerm:api:workflow-operator --request "POST /workflow_sessions" confirms the call is allowed).

q: I need to export all ~200,000 NERM profiles nightly. How should I page through /profiles?
must: use keyset paging with after_id (last id of the previous page), sorted by id ascending
after_id cannot be combined with offset, and other filters except profile_type_id/limit (and updated_after) are ignored or rejected
limit max 500 on /profiles (default 100); metadata=true returns _metadata with next/total; updated_after for incremental
must_not: says use filters= or count=true like ISC
says limit 250 or 10000 for NERM profiles
A: Use offset/limit paging on GET https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/profiles?limit=500&offset=0. Increase offset by limit until a page comes back with fewer than limit records or an empty profiles array. 500 is the practical maximum page size, which means about 400 calls for 200k profiles. Add filters to reduce volume, for example profile_type_id=<uuid> or status, and request only the attributes you need. Deep offsets get slow and are unstable if data changes during the run. So sort deterministically (order by id or created_at), and preferably run an incremental export using updated_at, or the 'after' / last-id cursor where it is available, instead of a full dump every night. Respect rate limits: on HTTP 429, back off and honour Retry-After. Parallelise moderately, partitioned by profile type. Write each page to staging and checkpoint the offset so a failed run can resume.
B: Use keyset paging with after_id, not offset. GET https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/profiles?limit=500&metadata=true (500 is the max on /profiles, default 100), then repeat with &after_id=<last id returned, or _metadata.after_id/next> until a page returns fewer than limit (or empty). after_id forces sorting by id ascending and cannot be combined with offset; other filters are ignored or rejected with 400 except profile_type_id and limit (so no status, name, archived alongside it). For a nightly delta, add updated_after=YYYY-MM-DD, which may be combined with after_id. Add exclude_attributes=true only if you don't need attribute values. Responses are {"profiles": [...], "_metadata": {limit, total, next, after_id}}. Don't use ISC-style count/sorters/filters parameters. No rate limits are documented, but back off on 429 and refresh the ISC JWT (expires about every 12 minutes) during a long run. ~200,000 profiles = about 400 calls.

q: I created a NERM workflow session with POST /workflow_sessions and it just sits there. Why?
must: the session only runs if ?run=true is passed (default false); otherwise it is saved
start it with PATCH /workflow_sessions/{id}?run=true (or create with run=true)
body is {"workflow_session": {workflow_id, requester_id, requester_type, ...}} with those three required; profile_id for update, profile_ids for batch
must_not: says sessions are queued for the daily automated run
A: POST /api/workflow_sessions only creates the session. Whether it runs depends on the workflow type and the payload. Common causes: (1) The workflow is a Create/Update request workflow whose first step is a form or request step that waits for human input, so it sits pending in the requester's/approver's queue. (2) It is waiting on an approval step, so check the approver's inbox. (3) You didn't supply required attributes or the profile reference (profile_id/uid for update workflows), so the step can't complete. (4) The workflow is inactive or the wrong workflow_id was used. (5) requester_id/requester_type (e.g. NeprofileUser) is invalid. Check GET /api/workflow_sessions/{id} and its status/current step in the UI under Workflows > Sessions. Use an Automated workflow, or provide all attributes in the body ("attributes":{...}), so that steps with no user interaction auto-advance.
B: Because POST /workflow_sessions does not start the workflow unless you add the query parameter run=true (default false). Without it you get a session in status new that just sits there. Either create with POST https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/workflow_sessions?run=true, or start the existing one with PATCH /api/workflow_sessions/{id}?run=true. Body must be wrapped: {"workflow_session": {"workflow_id": "<id>", "requester_id": "<user id>", "requester_type": "User", "profile_id": "<for update workflows>", "attributes": {...prefill by attribute uid}}}; workflow_id, requester_id and requester_type (User, NeprofileUser, NeaccessUser, NeaccessRegistrant) are required, profile_ids for batch workflows. Executing needs scope nerm:api:workflow-operator or nerm:general:manage (otherwise a generic 403). If it does run but stops later, look at status (pending_approval waits for an approver; failed can be a REST API step over 60 s) or a Close Session step. scripts/check_nerm.py flags sessions that will not start.

q: How do I find, via the NERM API, all non-terminated profiles whose first name starts with 'a'?
must: POST /advanced_search/run with {"advanced_search": {"condition_rules_attributes": [...]}}
a ProfileStatusRule with != Terminated plus a ProfileAttributeRule on the first-name attribute id with comparison_operator start_with?
attribute rules reference the attribute by id (condition_object_id) and its type (condition_object_type, e.g. TextFieldAttribute; the guide's examples use object_type NeAttribute)
must_not: uses a filters=firstName sw "a" query parameter
source: api/nerm/v1/pagination-metadata-filtering advanced search; NERM OpenAPI rule schemas
A: Use advanced search; there is no filters= expression on /profiles. First get the id of the first-name attribute (uid personal_first_name) with GET https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/ne_attributes (the rule needs the attribute id). Then POST /api/advanced_search/run?limit=500&offset=0 with {"advanced_search": {"condition_rules_attributes": [{"type": "ProfileStatusRule", "comparison_operator": "!=", "value": "Terminated"}, {"type": "ProfileAttributeRule", "condition_object_type": "TextFieldAttribute", "condition_object_id": "<attribute id>", "comparison_operator": "start_with?", "value": "a"}]}}. All rules must match (AND). The spec uses condition_object_type = the attribute's type; the guide's examples use "object_type": "NeAttribute" (check_nerm.py accepts both and warns). The response is {"profiles": [...]}; page with limit/offset. Add a ProfileTypeRule (== profile type id) to restrict to non-employees. To reuse it, save with POST /advanced_search and run with GET /advanced_search/{id}/run. Needs a scope that reads advanced search (profile-reader, profile-manager, workflow-operator, read-only).
B: Use the profile search/advanced query endpoint rather than a plain GET with query string filters. POST https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/advanced_search/run (or the profiles query endpoint). Body example: {"advanced_search":{"condition_rules_attributes":[{"type":"ProfileTypeRule","comparison_operator":"==","value":"<profile_type_id>"},{"type":"ProfileAttributeRule","condition_object_id":"<attribute id of personal_first_name>","object_type":"NeAttribute","comparison_operator":"starts_with","value":"a"},{"type":"ProfileStatusRule","comparison_operator":"!=","value":"Terminated"}]}} with limit/offset for paging. A simpler alternative is to GET /api/profiles?status=Active (also add OnLeave/Pending if you need them) and filter first names client-side, case-insensitively, since the match may be case-sensitive. Remember that 'non-terminated' includes Active, Inactive, On Leave and Pending.

q: What is the difference between SailPoint NERM and the Non-Employee Lifecycle Management in Identity Security Cloud?
must: NELM is built into ISC: non-employee sources and records with approvals, API /non-employee-sources, /non-employee-records on api.identitynow.com
NERM is a separate add-on product (ex SecZetta) on {tenant}.nonemployee.com with its own API, profile types/relationships, configurable workflows, external portal and risk scoring
NERM profiles reach ISC through the NERM connector as a source (identities)
must_not: says they are the same product or the same API
A: SailPoint NERM (Non-Employee Risk Management, from the SecZetta acquisition) is a separate product on its own tenant ({tenant}.nonemployee.com). It is a full system of record for third parties. It has configurable profile types (people and non-people: vendors, assets, devices), relationships between profiles, multi-step workflows (create/update/automated, approvals, vendor-portal/delegated collaboration, REST API steps), risk scoring, attestations/reviews, and its own REST API. It integrates with ISC through a NERM source/connector. ISC Non-Employee Lifecycle Management (NELM) is a lighter feature built into ISC. You define Non-Employee sources with up to 50 sources and a fixed attribute schema plus a few custom ones. Records are created manually, by CSV upload, or via the /non-employee-records API, with simple approval flows. Those records become identities through aggregation. There are no risk scores, no organisation/vendor portals, and no complex workflows. Choose NELM for simple contractor onboarding and NERM for heavy third-party risk and vendor management.
B: They are different products. NERM (Non-Employee Risk Management, formerly SecZetta) is a separate SaaS add-on at https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com with its own API (/api/profiles, /api/workflow_sessions...). It models any number of profile types (people, organizations, jobs, assignments, assets) with custom attributes and relationships, has configurable lifecycle workflows (create, update, batch, automated) and collaboration workflows for an external portal (registration, login, password reset) with 25+ action types, and per-attribute risk scoring. Non-Employee Lifecycle Management (NELM) is a feature inside ISC itself: non-employee sources with their own schema and records, a simple request/approval flow by account managers, no risk scoring, and its API on https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com (/non-employee-sources, /non-employee-records, /non-employee-requests, /non-employee-approvals). SailPoint positions NELM as the basic option and NERM for automation, self-service onboarding, delegated administration and external portals. NERM can feed ISC: person profiles become identities through the NERM connector, and ISC PATs authenticate to the NERM API.

q: How is a profile's overall risk score calculated in NERM, and which attributes can carry risk?
must: only option-based attributes: drop-down, check boxes, radio buttons, profile search, profile select (inherited only for profile search/select)
overall score = average of the average impact and the average probability (0-10, two decimals); a linked/inherited profile with higher risk overrides
risk is disabled by default and enabled per profile type; mitigation attributes reduce risk
must_not: says text fields or dates can carry risk
says overall is the sum or the maximum of all attributes
A: In NERM, risk is defined on attributes. Admins mark attributes as risk-relevant and assign a risk score/weight to each possible value, for example citizenship, background-check result, access to sensitive data, or location. Typically these are selection-type attributes (single/multi select, checkbox, radio), but the profile's risk level can also be set by a workflow. A profile's overall risk score is computed from the risk values of its scored attributes. Each attribute contributes its value's score times the attribute weight, and the result is normalised to the configured scale and mapped to risk levels (Low/Medium/High/Critical) through thresholds set per profile type. Risk can also roll up through relationships, so a person inherits part of the risk of their vendor/organisation profile. The score recalculates whenever a scored attribute changes. It is exposed on the profile (risk_score/risk_level) and can drive workflow conditions, reviews and ISC policies via sync.
B: Risk scoring is off by default and enabled per profile type, on a 0-10 scale with default levels Low/Medium/High (/risk_levels). Only option-based attributes can carry risk: drop-down, check boxes, radio buttons, profile search and profile select (text, date etc. cannot). Each attribute gets a risk type: Impact, Probability, Impact and Probability, Inherited (only profile search/select: takes the linked profile's risk) or None, with values per option; mitigation attributes can lower an attribute's risk. Overall score = average of (average impact score, average probability score), rounded to two decimals. If an inherited (linked) profile has a higher score, it overrides and raises the profile's score. Subcategories are displayed but do not change the score. Via API: GET /api/risk_scores returns objects of type Profile or WorkflowSession with overall, impact and probability scores and level ids; advanced search can filter with a RiskRule (secondary_value OverallRisk, operators ==, >, <).

q: We sync NERM non-employees to ISC. Which attribute correlates the accounts, which profiles get aggregated, and do all attributes sync?
must: Non-Employee Profile ID is aggregated automatically and mapped to Employee Number; default correlation Non-Employee Profile ID = Employee Number
only person profile types (core Non-Employees, custom employee/non-employee categories); status filter All or Active (Active + On Leave); archived profiles never aggregated
only mapped core attributes sync (First Name, Last Name, Business Email required); extended attributes do not; schema attributes are strings, no entitlement aggregation
must_not: says correlation is on email by default
says terminated/archived profiles are aggregated by default as active
A: The SailPoint Non-Employee Risk Management connector aggregates profiles as accounts. Non-Employee Profile ID is aggregated automatically and mapped to Employee Number; default correlation is Non-Employee Profile ID = Employee Number (changing it can create duplicate identities). First Name, Last Name and Business Email are required core attributes. Only person profile types (core Non-Employees, custom employee/non-employee categories, plus assignments as additional accounts correlated through their profile search/select attribute) are synced; enable it per type in NERM Admin > System > Identity Security Cloud Connection Settings (NON-EMPLOYEE / ASSIGNMENT tab). The source status filter is All or Active (Active + On Leave); archived profiles are never aggregated. Not all attributes sync: only those in the account schema (all strings), extended attributes do not sync, and entitlement aggregation is not supported for profile sources. Make only person profiles authoritative. API side: /api/isc/accounts and /api/profile_types/{id}/synced_attributes. NERM users and roles go through the separate NERM Users connector (matched on sailpoint_identity_id).
B: Use the SailPoint NERM source in ISC, configured with the NERM tenant URL and an API token. The account identity/correlation attribute is the NERM profile id (uid), typically correlated to an ISC identity attribute through the email or an employee/uid attribute in the correlation config. Usually you correlate on profile id for the native identity and on email for identity correlation. Only profiles of the profile types selected in the source configuration get aggregated, normally the people types such as Contractor, not vendors or assets. Often only certain statuses are included (exclude Terminated if filtered). Not all attributes sync. Only attributes mapped in the NERM source account schema / attribute mapping come across: standard name/email/status/manager plus the attributes you add. Reference attributes arrive as ids or names. ISC can also push attributes back (writeback) only for mapped fields. Run full aggregation on a schedule and use NERM-triggered events for near-real-time updates.

q: In a NERM automated workflow I put Status Change to Terminated before the manager approval step and a REST API step that calls a slow service. Any problem?
must: Status Change takes effect immediately, so the profile is terminated before approval: move it after the approval
REST API action times out after 60 seconds and the workflow session fails
automated workflows run once a day at a fixed, region-dependent time (not on demand)
must_not: says status change waits for the approval automatically
A: Yes, two. Status Change applies immediately when the step runs: placed before the approval, the profile is set to Terminated even if the manager later rejects. Move Status Change after the approval step. The REST API step times out after 60 seconds and the workflow session then fails, so a slow service will break the run; make the call fast (have the service accept and process asynchronously) or move the slow work outside NERM. Also remember automated workflows have no button: they run once a day at a fixed time set by the tenant's AWS region (not changeable), and select profiles with filters that must all match (e.g. end date reached), so an approval step means the session waits in pending_approval until the manager acts. A Close Session step ends the workflow and nothing after it runs.
B: Yes, there are two problems. (1) Order: setting Status to Terminated before the manager approval means the profile is terminated and, via the ISC sync, access is deprovisioned before anyone approves. If the manager rejects, you have to reverse it manually. Put the approval step first, then branch on its outcome, then do the Status Change. Also note that a terminated profile may fall out of scope for later steps and notifications. (2) The REST API step is synchronous with a timeout of roughly 30 seconds. A slow service can time out and fail the step, which stops or errors the workflow session. Make the downstream call asynchronous: have the service accept the request and return 200/202 quickly, then do the work and call back into the NERM API, for example by updating the profile or starting another workflow session. Also configure error handling or a failure branch, and keep the step idempotent in case it is retried.
